# #2208: Patch: a practice game that earns lets the AI finish every move, so a slow device no longer forfeits the reward
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
A signed-in player's practice game can pay Jlore and XP. The computer opponent thinks inside the player's browser, and the browser stops each of its moves after a second and a half. Afterwards the server checks the game by working every AI move out again with no time limit, and pays nothing if any move comes out different. So on a slow phone, or in a long game on any device, a won game can pay nothing, and the result only says that the AI chose another move on the server. Once this is built, a game that earns lets the AI finish each move, which may take a moment longer on a slow phone. If a move still has to be cut short, the result says the device ran out of time instead of blaming the server.

## Why
- Every practice AI decision is cut at `PRACTICE_AI_CLOCK_MS`, earning games included. `apps/web/src/practice/core.ts:476-480` passes `deadlineMs: t0 + PRACTICE_AI_CLOCK_MS`, and `apps/web/src/practice/config.ts:37` sets it to 1500.
- R1303002 (`spec/rulings/R1303002.md`) re-runs each AI move of a claim at `AI_BUDGET` with no clock. A move the browser cut short to a different one makes the claim pay nothing. That rule is deliberate, so the client cannot weaken the AI, and this change keeps it.
- Moves already come near the cap on the development machine. `training/history/improve-cycle-2026-10-16.md:63-66` records 12,901 decisions averaging 138.5 ms. Three games had a 95th-percentile move of 1,000 ms or more, and one game had a line at 2,000 ms or more.
- The browser runs the same search as WebAssembly. `docs/polish/3-ai.md:1515-1518` estimates that one `reduce` costs a mid-range phone 3 to 5 times what it costs the development machine.
- The timing gate allows a native decision up to 1,500 ms (`crates/ai/src/gate.rs:144`, `max_decision_ms`), the same as the browser's cap. So it never flags a decision that a slower device will cut.
- The worker already knows when a cut happens: each decision reports `stoppedBy: 'clock'` (`apps/web/src/wire/ai.ts:89`, `crates/ai/src/types.rs:120-124`). The game still claims, and the dialog then shows the server's `ai_mismatch` as `the AI chose another move on the server` (`apps/web/src/practice/earning.ts:67-68`). That names the symptom, not the cause.

## Proposal
1. A game with `earning: true` uses a new named cap, `PRACTICE_EARNING_AI_CLOCK_MS` in `apps/web/src/practice/config.ts`, set many times `PRACTICE_AI_CLOCK_MS`. It is only a backstop for a stuck worker; the node budget, which is what the server replays, stays the real bound. Free games without a server seed, lessons and sandbox games keep the 1,500 ms cap.
2. When a decision of an earning game still reports `stoppedBy: 'clock'`, the worker marks the game. The mark is saved with the game, so a game resumed after a reload knows it too.
3. The claim is still sent, because a cut move often matches the full one. If the server refuses it as `ai_mismatch` and the game carries the mark, the result dialog says the device took too long over one of the AI's moves. Every other refusal reads as it does today.
4. A ruling in this issue's block for the earning cap and the mark. §9.9's budgets paragraph names both, beside its sentence that the browser adds a wall-clock cap a claim does not replay.

## Where it lands
- Web: `apps/web/src/practice/core.ts`, `config.ts`, `earning.ts`, the save (`saveStore.ts`, `resume.ts`), `PracticeResult.tsx`, and the zh-CN strings.
- Tests: `apps/web/src/practice/core.test.ts`, `earning.test.ts`, `resume.test.ts`.
- Spec: SPEC §9.9 (`spec/09-architecture.md`) and §14.8 (`spec/14-economy.md`), R1303002, and a new note in `spec/rulings/` with its paragraph in `spec/pending/<issue>.md`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An earning game's `decide` call carries the earning cap. A free game without a server seed, a lesson and a sandbox game carry `PRACTICE_AI_CLOCK_MS`.
- [ ] A fake clock cuts one decision of an earning game. The game is marked, the mark survives a resume, and an `ai_mismatch` refusal shows the device line.
- [ ] A refusal for any other reason shows its own text, as now.
- [ ] A test is named after the new ruling and listed in its `proven_in`, and `cargo jackioh spec check` is green.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/practice` and `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` are green. The new cap is a named constant that nothing else states.
- [ ] The server's re-run is unchanged, and `crates/server/tests/api/practice.rs` passes untouched.

## Size and risks
Medium: about six web files and a ruling. Nothing changes on the server or in the AI.
- On a slow phone the AI's turn takes visibly longer in an earning game. The thinking indicator (`ThinkIndicator.tsx`) already covers the wait, the worker keeps the page responsive, and the backstop cap still bounds a stuck worker.
- The repo holds no WebAssembly or phone timings, so how often claims fail today is not measured. The native numbers above are a lower bound.
